items.samhita_patha: सू॒नृता॒ संन॑तिः॒ क्षेमः॑ स्व॒धोर्जामृतं॒ सहः॑। उच्छि॑ष्टे॒ सर्वे॑ प्र॒त्यञ्चः॒ कामाः॒ कामे॑न तातृपुः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Pleasantness, compliance ( sáṁnati ), comfort ( kṣéma ), custom (? svadhā́ ), refreshment, immortality, power—in the remnant all occurring ( pratyáñc ) desires are satisfied with desire.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads at the end tṛmpanti . Most of the pada -mss. and many of the saṁhitā -mss. read simply kṣéma in a (including our Bp.O.D.R.K.Kp.).

items.samhita_patha_plain: सूनृता संनतिः क्षेमः स्वधोर्जामृतं सहः। उच्छिष्टे सर्वे प्रत्यञ्चः कामाः कामेन तातृपुः ॥

items.samhita_patha: नव॒ भूमीः॑ समु॒द्रा उच्छि॑ष्टेऽधि॑ श्रि॒ता दिवः॑। आ॒ सूर्यो॑ भा॒त्युच्छि॑ष्टेऽहोरा॒त्रे अपि॒ तन्मयि॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: The nine earths, oceans, skies, are set ( çritá ) in the remnant; the sun shines in the remnant; day-and-night: also that in me.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -mss. in general read simply çritā́ (or çṛtā́ ) in b . Two or three mss. (including our O.) read ‘pi in d . Ppp. reads in a, b bhūmyāṁ samudrasyo ’chiṣṭe , and has ca for api in d . ⌊The comm. treats the last words of the vs. as under vs. 12.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: नव भूमीः समुद्रा उच्छिष्टेऽधि श्रिता दिवः। आ सूर्यो भात्युच्छिष्टेऽहोरात्रे अपि तन्मयि ॥

items.samhita_patha: उ॑प॒हव्यं॑ विषू॒वन्तं॒ ये च॑ य॒ज्ञा गुहा॑ हि॒ताः। बिभ॑र्ति भ॒र्ता विश्व॒स्योच्छि॑ष्टो जनि॒तुः पि॒ता ॥

commentaries.whitney: The added oblation ( upahávya ), the dividing [day], and the sacrifices that are put in secret, the remnant bears, bearer of all, father of the generator.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads divi çrutaḥ ⌊intending çritāḥ? ⌋ for guhā hitāḥ in b . The mss. are divided between upahávyam and upahavyám; the latter is read by our B.W.O.s.m.D.R.T.; and K. has -havyàm .

items.samhita_patha_plain: उपहव्यं विषूवन्तं ये च यज्ञा गुहा हिताः। बिभर्ति भर्ता विश्वस्योच्छिष्टो जनितुः पिता ॥

items.samhita_patha: पि॒ता ज॑नि॒तुरुच्छि॒ष्टोऽसोः॒ पौत्रः॑ पिताम॒हः। स क्षि॑यति॒ विश्व॒स्येशा॑नो॒ वृषा॒ भूम्या॑मति॒घ्न्यः᳡ ॥

commentaries.whitney: The remnant, father of the generator, of breath ( ásu ) the grandson, grandfather—he dwells, ruler of all, an overpowering (? atighnyà ) bull upon the earth.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in b ‘sāu putraç ca , which, without the ca , is an acceptable improvement.

items.samhita_patha_plain: पिता जनितुरुच्छिष्टोऽसोः पौत्रः पितामहः। स क्षियति विश्वस्येशानो वृषा भूम्यामतिघ्न्यः᳡ ॥

items.samhita_patha: ऋ॒तं स॒त्यं तपो॑ रा॒ष्ट्रं श्रमो॒ धर्म॑श्च॒ कर्म॑ च। भू॒तं भ॑वि॒ष्यदुच्छि॑ष्टे वी॒र्यं᳡ ल॒क्ष्मीर्बलं॒ बले॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Righteousness, truth, penance, kingship, toil, and virtue ( dhárma ) and deed ( kárman ), being ( bhūtá ), what will be, [is] in the remnant; heroism, fortune ( lakṣmī́ ), strength in strength.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has dīkṣā for rāṣṭram in a : a better reading. The comm. explains ṛta here by manasā yathārthasaṁkalpanam 'right conception'; bale at the end he makes = balavati tasminn ucchiṣṭe .

items.samhita_patha_plain: ऋतं सत्यं तपो राष्ट्रं श्रमो धर्मश्च कर्म च। भूतं भविष्यदुच्छिष्टे वीर्यं᳡ लक्ष्मीर्बलं बले ॥

commentaries.whitney: Success, force, design, dominion, kingship, the six wide [quarters], the year [is] in the remnant, íḍā , the orders ( prāiṣá ), the dips ( gráha ), the oblation.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines ojā ”hūtiḥ in a . ⌊W. interlines 'potions' as an alternative for 'dips.'⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: समृद्धिरोज आकूतिः क्षत्रं राष्ट्रं षडुर्व्यः᳡। संवत्सरोऽध्युच्छिष्ट इडा प्रैषा ग्रहा हविः ॥

items.samhita_patha: चतु॑र्होतार आ॒प्रिय॑श्चातुर्मा॒स्यानि॑ नी॒विदः॑। उच्छि॑ष्टे य॒ज्ञा होत्राः॑ पशुब॒न्धास्तदिष्ट॑यः ॥
items.pada_patha: चतु॑:ऽहोतार: । आ॒प्रिय॑ । चा॒तु॒:ऽमा॒स्यानि॑ । नि॒ऽविद॑: । उत्ऽशि॑ष्टे । य॒ज्ञा: । होत्रा॑: । प॒शु॒ऽब॒न्धा: । तत् । इष्ट॑य: ॥९.१९॥

commentaries.whitney: The four-priest ( cátur-hotṛ ) [sacrifices], the āprī́s , the seasonal [oblations], the nivíds —in the remnant [are] the sacrifices, the invocations, the victim-offerings ( paçubandhá ), then the offerings ( íṣṭi ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Tádiṣṭayaḥ at the end in our edition is a misprint for tád íṣṭayaḥ .

items.samhita_patha_plain: चतुर्होतार आप्रियश्चातुर्मास्यानि नीविदः। उच्छिष्टे यज्ञा होत्राः पशुबन्धास्तदिष्टयः ॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॑र्धमा॒साश्च॒ मासा॑श्चार्त॒वा ऋ॒तुभिः॑ स॒ह। उच्छि॑ष्टे घो॒षिणी॒रापः॑ स्तनयि॒त्नुः श्रुति॑र्म॒ही ॥

commentaries.whitney: Both the half-months and the months, the year-divisions ( ārtavá ) with the seasons; in the remnant [are] the noisy waters, the thunder, the great sound (? çrúti ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. reads çuci in d , so we lack his conjecture as to the meaning of çruti .

items.samhita_patha_plain: अर्धमासाश्च मासाश्चार्तवा ऋतुभिः सह। उच्छिष्टे घोषिणीरापः स्तनयित्नुः श्रुतिर्मही ॥

commentaries.whitney: Success ( rā́ddhi ), attainment, obtainment, permeation, greatness, prosperity ⌊ edhatú ⌋—in the remnant over-attainment and growth ( bhū́ti ) [is] put in, put down, put.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Several of our mss. (P.M.W.I.O.) accent vyā́pti in b . All the mss. save one or two (including our B.) leave edhatuḥ unaccented, as if it were taken for a 3d dual perfect; both editions read edhatúḥ . The comm. strangely reads at the end hitāḥ; ⌊but the pada -text makes all three words of d singular⌋.

commentaries.whitney: Both what breathes with breath and what sees with sight: from the remnant were born all the gods in heaven, heaven-resorters.

commentaries.whitney: The verses ( ṛ́c ), the chants, the meters, the ancient ( purāṇá ), together with the formula ( yájus ): from the remnant were born etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, for ṛcaḥ sāmāni, ṛgyajussāmāni , and also prefixes to the verse our 27 a, b (combining devāṣ pit- ).

commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -mss. (save one of SPP's) divide evā́stām in a into evá: ā́stām , and the accent of the verb is perfectly defensible, though SPP. alters to āstām . Some of the mss. (including our Bp.P.M.E.) leave mahati unaccented: cf. vs. 6 b , and iii. 6. 3.

commentaries.whitney: Ten gods were born together from gods of old; whoever may know them plainly, he verily may talk big to-day.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'May teach the unlimited brahman ' is the comm's understanding of the last clause.

commentaries.whitney_notes: The first half-verse occurs also as 7. 25 a, b above, and the first three pādas as vs. 26 a, b, c below. Ppp. combines vā ”kūtim in d .

items.samhita_patha: येत आसी॒द्भूमिः॒ पूर्वा॒ याम॑द्धा॒तय॒ इद्वि॒दुः। यो वै तां॑ वि॒द्यान्ना॒मथा॒ स म॑न्येत पुराण॒वित् ॥

commentaries.whitney:
The earth that was previous to this one ( itás ), which the sages
( addhātí ) indeed knew—whoever may know that by name, he may think himself knowing in ancient things.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation implies emendation of tā́n in c to tā́ṁ , which SPP. gives in his text, with about half of his mss. Ppp's version is quite different; it reads for a ye ’to bhūmiṣ pūrvā ”sit; and, for c, d , ke tasyan devā ”sate kasinin sā ’dhi çrutaḥ ⌊intending tasyām and çritā? ⌋.

items.samhita_patha_plain: येत आसीद्भूमिः पूर्वा यामद्धातय इद्विदुः। यो वै तां विद्यान्नामथा स मन्येत पुराणवित् ॥

items.samhita_patha: कुत॒ इन्द्रः॒ कुतः॒ सोमः॒ कुतो॑ अ॒ग्निर॑जायत। कुत॒स्त्वष्टा॒ सम॑भव॒त्कुतो॑ धा॒ताजा॑यत ॥

commentaries.whitney: Whence was Indra, whence Soma, whence Agni born? whence did Tvashṭar come into being? whence was Dhātar born?
commentaries.whitney_notes: [ Kāurupathi.—catustriṅçat. adhyātmamanyudāivatam. ānuṣṭubham: 33. pathyāpan̄kti. ] Found also (except vss. 33, 34) in Pāipp. xvi. (in the verse-order 1-6, 8-10, 7, 12, 11, 13, 15, 14, 16-32). ⌊The hymn is noticed neither by Kāuç. nor by Vāit.⌋ Translated: Ludwig, p. 402; Scherman, p. 67 (8 vss.); Deussen, Geschichte , i. 1. 270-277 (with introduction and interpretation); Henry, 123, 160; Griffith, ii. 80. Ppp. has for d dhātā sam abhavat kutaḥ .

items.samhita_patha_plain: कुत इन्द्रः कुतः सोमः कुतो अग्निरजायत। कुतस्त्वष्टा समभवत्कुतो धाताजायत ॥

commentaries.whitney: From Indra Indra, from Soma Soma, from Agni Agni was born; Tvashṭar was born from Tvashṭar; from Dhātar Dhātar was born.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. arranges in d dhātā dhātur .

items.samhita_patha: ये त आस॒न्दश॑ जा॒ता दे॒वा दे॒वेभ्यः॑ पु॒रा। पु॒त्रेभ्यो॑ लो॒कं द॒त्त्वा कस्मिं॒स्ते लो॒क आ॑सते ॥

commentaries.whitney: The ten gods that were of old, born from gods—having given the world to [their] sons, in what world sit they?
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines tā ”san in a , and reads puraḥ for purā in b . ⌊For consistency, the Berlin ed. should have dattvā́ .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: ये त आसन्दश जाता देवा देवेभ्यः पुरा। पुत्रेभ्यो लोकं दत्त्वा कस्मिंस्ते लोक आसते ॥

commentaries.whitney: When he brought hair, bone, sinew, flesh, marrow, having made a body with feet, what world did he afterward enter?
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. reads sam abharat in b .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यदा केशानस्थि स्नाव मांसं मज्जानमाभरत्। शरीरं कृत्वा पादवत्कं लोकमनु प्राविशत् ॥

items.samhita_patha: कुतः॒ केशा॒न्कुतः॒ स्नाव॒ कुतो॒ अस्थी॒न्याभ॑रत्। अङ्गा॒ पर्वा॑णि म॒ज्जानं॒ को मां॒सं कुत॒ आभ॑रत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Whence brought he the hair, whence the sinew, whence the bones? the limbs, the joints, the marrow, the flesh who brought from whence?
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines at the end kutā ”bharat . The comm. appears again to read sam abharat at end of b . A few mss. (including our Bp.R.) read snā́vaḥ in a .

items.samhita_patha_plain: कुतः केशान्कुतः स्नाव कुतो अस्थीन्याभरत्। अङ्गा पर्वाणि मज्जानं को मांसं कुत आभरत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Pourers-together namely are those gods who brought together the bringings-together; having poured together the whole mortal, the gods entered man.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads çaṅsatas for saṁsicas in a , and saṁsṛjya for saṁsicya in c .

items.samhita_patha: ऊ॒रू पादा॑वष्ठी॒वन्तौ॒ शिरो॒ हस्ता॒वथो॒ मुख॑म्। पृ॒ष्टीर्ब॑र्जह्ये᳡ पा॒र्श्वे कस्तत्सम॑दधा॒दृषिः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney:
Thighs, feet, knee-joints, head, hands, also face, ribs, nipples
(? barjahyà ), sides: what seer put that together?
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. has nothing to say for barjahyè except 'the parts so called.' Ppp. reads instead majjahye; and it has çroṇī for çiras in b . It also makes our 14 c, d and 15 c, d exchange places.

commentaries.whitney: Head, hands, also face, tongue and neck, vertebræ—all that, having enveloped with skin, the great putting-together put together.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads ⌊ bāhu for mukham in a and has⌋ in c tat sarvam . The comm. paraphrases saṁdhā in d with saṁdhānakartrī devatā .

commentaries.whitney: The great body which lay there, put together by the putting-together—who brought into it the color with which it shines ( ruc ) here today?
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads adadhat for açayat in a , mayi for mahat in b , and ko ‘smin in d . SPP. reports all his pada -mss. as having at the end ā॰ábharat , which he emends to ā́: abharat; our pada -mss. give the latter.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यत्तच्छरीरमशयत्संधया संहितं महत्। येनेदमद्य रोचते को अस्मिन्वर्णमाभरत् ॥

items.samhita_patha: सर्वे॑ दे॒वा उपा॑शिक्ष॒न्तद॑जानाद्व॒धूः स॒ती। ई॒शा वश॑स्य॒ या जा॒या सास्मि॒न्वर्ण॒माभ॑रत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: All the gods assisted (? upa-çikṣ ); that she who was a woman knew; she who was wife of control (? váça ), mistress ( īçā́ ), brought color into it.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in a upāsikṣan , and viṣasya for vaçasya in c ; the comm. (with two or three of SPP's mss.) has instead of the latter viçvasya . There are, failing help from sense, various questionable points in the construction.

commentaries.whitney: When Tvashṭar bored through [him?] who [was] the superior father of Tvashṭar, having made the mortal a house, the gods entered into man.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Probably c is adjunct of devā́s; whether b is object of the verb in a is more doubtful. Ppp. gives no help. The comm. makes b define Tvaṣṭar himself, and understands the 'boring' of the openings for the senses, the eyes and ears etc. ⌊Ludwig renders c : "machten die götter den sterblichen zu [ihrem] hause."⌋

items.samhita_patha: स्वप्नो॒ वै त॒न्द्रीर्निरृ॑तिः पा॒प्मानो॒ नाम॑ दे॒वताः॑। ज॒रा खाल॑त्यं॒ पालि॑त्यं॒ शरी॑र॒मनु॒ प्रावि॑शन् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Sleep, weariness, misery ( nírṛti ), the deities named evils, old age, baldness, hoariness, entered the body afterward ( ánu ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. reads tandrī in a , and khālityam in c . Anu perhaps rather 'one after another.'

commentaries.whitney: Theft, ill-doing, wrong, truth, sacrifice, great glory, both strength, dominion, and force, entered the body afterward.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. has the better reading sahas for bṛhat in b .

commentaries.whitney: Both growth ( bhū́ti ) and diminution, generosities and niggardlinesses, both hungerings and all thirstings, entered the body afterward.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines vā ’bhūtiç in a .

commentaries.whitney: Both revilings and non-revilings, both what [says] "come on" ( hánta ) and "no," faith, the sacrificial fee, and non-faith, entered the body afterward.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines vā ’nindāç in a . The majority of mss. (including our Bp.B.P.M.E.T.R.K.) read dakṣiṇā́ in c ; ⌊if I understand W's Collation Book, only Bp.T.K. among his mss. are noted as so reading;⌋ both editions give dákṣiṇā . The comm. explains the word as meaning dhanasamṛddhi . ⌊Cf. Oldenberg, ZDMG. l. 449.⌋

commentaries.whitney:
Both knowledges and ignorances, and what else is to be taught
( upa-diç ); the bráhman entered the body; the verses, the chant, also the formula.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines vā ’vidyāç in a , and reads for c çarīraṁ sarve prā ’viçan ⌊= our 25 c ⌋. Bráhman perhaps is here the 'charm,' representing the Atharvan hymns.

commentaries.whitney: Delights, joys, enjoyments, and they that enjoy enjoyments, laughter, sport, dances, entered the body afterward.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads for a ānandā nandāṣ pramado . The comm. reads nur iṣṭās in c ⌊see SPP's note, p. 163⌋. The first half-verse is identical with 7. 26 a, b above.

commentaries.whitney:
Both appeals ( ālāpá ) and pratings ( pralāpá ), and they who utter
( -lap ) addresses ( abhīlāpa- )—all entered the body, joiners-on ( āyúj ), joiners-forth ( prayúj ), joiners.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads prāyujas in d . The comm. explains the last words as = āyojanāni , prayojanāni , and yojanāni . The first half-verse is as it were a change rung on 24 a, b .

commentaries.whitney: Breath-and-expiration, sight, hearing, indestructibleness and destruction, out-breathing and up-breathing, speech, mind—they go about ( īja- ) with the body.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The first three pādas are the same with 4 a, b, c , above.

commentaries.whitney: Both blessings ( āçís ) and precepts ( praçís ), demands ( saṁçís ) and explanations ( viçís ), thoughts, all devisings, entered the body afterward.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. explains the difficult compounds of -çis as mechanically as those of -yuj in vs. 25: āçāsanāni , praçāsanāni , saṁçāsanāni , vividhāni çāsanāni .

items.samhita_patha: आस्ते॑यीश्च॒ वास्ते॑यीश्च त्वर॒णाः कृ॑प॒णाश्च॒ याः। गुह्याः॑ शु॒क्रा स्थू॒ला अ॒पस्ता बी॑भ॒त्साव॑सादयन् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Both those of the blood and those of the bladder, the hasting and those that are pitiable, the secret, the clear, the thick waters—those they caused to settle in the repugnant one.
commentaries.whitney_notes: That is, apparently, in the body that was loth to receive them. SPP. reads unaccountably at the beginning ā́steyīs , against the great majority of his mss., the comm., and the sense. The reading has not been noted at all among our mss., but sn and st are very imperfectly distinguished in general by the scribes, and the latter may possibly have been intended by some among them. The comm. derives the word from ā + snā , instead of from asan; the form in which he gives it is āsneyyas . The second word he reads vāsneyyas , and derives it from vā 'or' + snā! Then he adds another derivation for both words, from āsana 'sitting,' and vasna 'price' respectively. He reads then āpas in c . Ppp. reads çukriyā in c .

commentaries.whitney: Having made bone [their] fuel, then they caused eight waters to settle; having made seed [their] sacrificial butter, the gods entered man.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The first part of the verse is spoiled in Ppp. The comm. has the more regular accus. pl. apas in b (the pada -text aṣṭá: ā́paḥ , as required by the accent; the comm. in general pays no heed to accent). He acutely refers to Tāitt. Brāh. i. 1. 9 4 , where bone is identified with fuel, and seed with sacrificial butter.

commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Shared' ( ví bhejire , pl.) is ungrammatical as taken with the subject (which is only two-fold) given in the text. The comm. understands that the other 'senses' with their deities are viewed as included with these two. Ppp. reads tathā instead of atha in c .

commentaries.whitney: Therefore, indeed, one who knows man ⌊ púruṣa ⌋ thinks "this is bráhman "; for all deities are seated in him, as cows in a cow-stall.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Our text should read at the end ivā́ ”sate with SPP. and nearly all the mss. (our Bp.B. ivā ”sate ). Ppp. has a less naive d : çarīre ‘dhi samāhitaḥ .

commentaries.whitney: By the first dying, it goes apart dividing threefold: yonder goes it with one [part]; yonder goes it with one; here with one it dwells (? ni-sev ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse and the one following are (as above noted) wanting in Ppp. The comm. reads ni for vi in b . He regards the two 'yonders' as pointing respectively to heaven and hell, and paraphrases ni ṣevate by nitarāṁ sukhaduḥkhātmakān bhogān sevate . ⌊He makes jīvātmā the subject: and a masculine subject seems required by víṣvan̄ , unless we read ní just after it.⌋

commentaries.whitney: Within waters that are sluggish (? stīmá ), old, is the body placed; within that is might (? çáva , çávas ?); thence is it called might.
commentaries.whitney_notes: There is perhaps in c, d a play upon the word çávas , which may mean either 'might' (as neut.) or (as masc.) 'corpse.' The comm. paraphrases it both times with balātmakaḥ sūtrātmā ⌊i.e. the parameçvara⌋. He explains stīmāsu as anārdraṁ sarvaṁ jagad ārdraṁ kurvatīṣu . ⌊Here ends the fourth anuvāka , with 2 hymns and 61 verses. The quoted Anukr. says with reference to this eighth hymn "yan manyur" ity atra caturdaça ca: that is 14 over 20.⌋

commentaries.whitney: What arms ( bāhú ) [there are], what arrows, and the powers ( vīryà ) of bows, swords ( así ), axes ( paraçú ), weapon, and what thought-and-design in the heart—all that, O Arbudi, do thou make our enemies to see; and do thou show forth specters ( udārá ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. refers to AB. vi. 1, where Arbuda is named and called a serpent-sage, and declares Arbudi and Nyarbudi to be his two sons. Udārān he explains as udgatān antarikṣacarān rakṣaḥpiçācādīn mantrasāmarthyodbhāvitān , or also as sūryaraçmiprabhavā ulkādaya āntarikṣyā utpātāḥ , specters or portents. ⌊Pāda d , below, vs. 13 b .⌋

commentaries.whitney: Stand up, equip ye yourselves ( sam-nah ), O friends, god-folk; beheld, concealed of you be [those] who are our friends, O Arbudi.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The occurrence of mitrās m. and mitrāṇi n. in the same verse is puzzling, also the conjunction of saṁdṛṣṭa and gupta , and of vas with the singular arbude . The comm. reads saṁdṛṣṭās and guptās in c . Our Bp. reads yā́ḥ in d . ⌊Pāda a = 26 b and 10. 1 a .⌋ ⌊W. interlines "protected?" over "concealed."⌋

commentaries.whitney: Stand ye (two) up, take ye hold; with tying up, with tying together, gird ye the armies of our enemies, O Arbudi.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The dual verbs doubtless imply, as the comm. also points out, the inclusion of Nyarbudi in the address to Arbudi ⌊cf. vs. 11⌋. The comm. reads senām in c .

commentaries.whitney: The God that is Arbudi by name, and the lord ( ī́çāna ) Nyarbudi, by whom the atmosphere is involved ( ā-vṛ ), and this great earth—by those (two) who are allied with Indra, I go after what is conquered with an army.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Probably 'I follow up with my army what is already conquered by them.' The two last pādas are by the comm. reckoned as the first line of the next verse.

commentaries.whitney: Presenting to view, O Nyarbudi, the seven kinds of specters, with them all do thou stand up, when the butter is offered, with the army.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -text reads in a jātā́n: ni॰arbude; but the reading is plainly false, and should be either jātā́: ni॰arbude , or jātā́ni: arbude; either of these, considering that to the scribes nya and nnya are entirely equivalent and exchangeable (see my Skt. Gr. §§ 229, 232), would correctly represent the saṁhitā -reading. ⌊Cf. the reading of the comm. at 10. 21.⌋

commentaries.whitney: Smiting herself, tear-faced, and crop-eared (?), let her yell, with disheveled hair, when the man is slain, bitten (? rad ), O Arbudi, of thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'Her'—namely, the wife or sister or the like; more distinctly pointed to in the next verse. Radita ought to mean rather 'scraped' or 'scratched'; there seems to be no other example of it in the sense 'bitten': perhaps as a mere scratch from the fang of a serpent is enough to kill. The comm. takes radita as a noun (like ruta, stnita, citta , etc.), = dantāir vilekhane khādane sati . Of kṛdhukarṇ#i the comm. says: kṛdhv iti hrasvanāma: karṇābharaṇaparityāgena hrasvakarṇī . The verse is translated (also vs. 14, and 10. 7) by Bloomfield, in AJP. xi. 340.

items.samhita_patha: सं॒कर्ष॑न्ती क॒रूक॑रं॒ मन॑सा पु॒त्रमि॒च्छन्ती॑। पतिं॒ भ्रात॑र॒मात्स्वान्र॑दि॒ते अ॑र्बुदे॒ तव॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Drawing in her karū́kara , seeking with her mind her son, husband, brother, also her people ( svá )—in case of thy bite, O Arbudi.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The ending is the same with that of vs. 7, understood as the comm. takes it; we might also supply '[he being] bitten' etc. The Pet. Lex. renders karūkara 'vertebra of the neck and spine': rather (in ÇB. xii. 2. 4 10, 14 ), perhaps, 'a point or spinous process of a vertebra.' The comm. explains karu as an imitative word, and karūkara as meaning anything that makes the sound karu , and so designating hastapādādyavayavagataṁ saṁdhimad asthijātam; and he goes on loke hi bhayavaçād ubhayor hastayoḥ parasparān̄gulinipīḍanena tādṛçaṁ çabdam utpādayanti . This is far from relieving satisfactorily the obscurity. Most of our mss. accent svā̀n in c .

items.samhita_patha_plain: संकर्षन्ती करूकरं मनसा पुत्रमिच्छन्ती। पतिं भ्रातरमात्स्वान्रदिते अर्बुदे तव ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: सम्ऽकर्षन्ती । करूकरम् । मनसा । पुत्रम् । इच्छन्ती । पतिम् । भ्रातरम् । आत् । स्वान् । रदिते । अर्बुदे । तव ॥११.८॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॒लिक्ल॑वा जाष्कम॒दा गृध्राः॑ श्ये॒नाः प॑त॒त्त्रिणः॑। ध्वाङ्क्षाः॑ श॒कुन॑यस्तृप्यन्त्व॒मित्रे॑षु समी॒क्षय॑न्रदि॒ते अ॑र्बुदे॒ तव॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Let the buzzards, jāṣkamadás , vultures, falcons, winged ones, let the crows, the birds ( çakúni ), satisfy themselves—exhibiting among the enemies—in case of thy bite, O Arbudi.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This and the following hymn are wanting in Pāipp., although bits of vss. 15-17 of this one are to be found in Pāipp. xvii. The opening words of the two are quoted together in Kāuç. 16. 21, in connection with rites for insuring success in war. ⌊The use of the two hymns forms a sequel to the rites described in the introduction to viii. 8, which see; and cf. under viii. 8. 24.⌋ Translated: Ludwig, p. 530; Henry, 126, 164; Griffith, ii. 84; Bloomfield, 123, 631. We have here two refrain-phrases, neither of which stands in any grammatical connection with its surroundings (the pple. 'exhibiting' being nom. sing. masc). The comm. reads in a aliklabāḥ and yāḥ klamadāḥ; and some of the mss. have jāḥkam- (so our B.O.s.m.).

items.samhita_patha_plain: अलिक्लवा जाष्कमदा गृध्राः श्येनाः पतत्त्रिणः। ध्वाङ्क्षाः शकुनयस्तृप्यन्त्वमित्रेषु समीक्षयन्रदिते अर्बुदे तव ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: अलिक्लवा: । जाष्कमदा: । गृध्रा: । श्येना: । पतत्रिण: । ध्वाङ्क्षा: । शकुनय: । तृप्यन्तु । अमित्रेषु । सम्ऽईक्षयन् । रदिते । अर्बुदे । तव ॥११.९॥

items.samhita_patha: अथो॒ सर्वं॒ श्वाप॑दं॒ मक्षि॑का तृप्यतु॒ क्रिमिः॑। पौरु॑षे॒येऽधि॒ कुण॑पे रदि॒ते अ॑र्बुदे॒ तव॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Then let all wild beasts, let the fly, let the worm satisfy itself upon the carrion of men, bitten, O Arbudi, of thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Here the refrain stands again in grammatical connection.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अथो सर्वं श्वापदं मक्षिका तृप्यतु क्रिमिः। पौरुषेयेऽधि कुणपे रदिते अर्बुदे तव ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: अथो इति । सर्वम् । श्वापदम् । मक्षिका । तृप्यतु । क्रिमि: । पौरुषेये । अधि । कुणपे । रदिते । अर्बुदे । तव ॥११.१०॥

items.samhita_patha: आ गृ॑ह्णीतं॒ सं बृ॑हतं प्राणापा॒नान्न्य॑र्बुदे। नि॑वा॒शा घोषाः॒ सं य॑न्त्व॒मित्रे॑षु समी॒क्षय॑न्रदि॒ते अ॑र्बुदे॒ तव॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Take ye (two) hold, tear out ( sam-bṛh ) [their] breath-and-expiration, O Nyarbudi; let groaning (? nivāçá ) noises assemble—exhibiting among the enemies—in case of thy bite, O Arbudi.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Again (as in vs. 3) the other serpent-deity is included in a in the invocation ⌊this time of Nyarbudi⌋. The comm. reads vṛhatam in a . He explains nivāçās as nīcīnaṁ vāçyamānā ābhāṣyamāṇāḥ .

items.samhita_patha_plain: आ गृह्णीतं सं बृहतं प्राणापानान्न्यर्बुदे। निवाशा घोषाः सं यन्त्वमित्रेषु समीक्षयन्रदिते अर्बुदे तव ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: निऽवाशा: । घोषा: । सम् । यन्तु । अमित्रेषु । सम्ऽईक्षयन् । रदिते । अर्बुदे । तव ॥१.११॥

items.samhita_patha: उद्वे॑पय॒ सं वि॑जन्तां भिया॒मित्रा॒न्त्सं सृ॑ज। उ॑रुग्रा॒हैर्बा॑ह्व॒ङ्कैर्विध्या॑मित्रान्न्यर्बुदे ॥

commentaries.whitney: Make thou [them] tremble; let them quake together; unite our enemies with fear; with broad-gripping arm-hooks pierce thou our enemies, O Nyarbudi.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. reads in c ūrugrāhāis (which is not bad) and bāhuvan̄kāis , explaining the latter by bāhunā vakrabandhanāiḥ . Our P.M.W. read at the end amítrāṇy arbude: compare 6 a , above.

items.samhita_patha_plain: उद्वेपय सं विजन्तां भियामित्रान्त्सं सृज। उरुग्राहैर्बाह्वङ्कैर्विध्यामित्रान्न्यर्बुदे ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: उत् । वेपय । सम् । विजन्ताम् । भिया । अमित्रान् । सम् । सृज । उरुऽग्राहै: । बाहुऽअङ्कै: । विध्य । अमित्रान् । निऽअर्बुदे ॥११.१२॥

items.samhita_patha: मुह्य॑न्त्वेषां बा॒हव॑श्चित्ताकू॒तं च॒ यद्धृ॒दि। मैषा॒मुच्छे॑षि॒ किं च॒न र॑दि॒ते अ॑र्बुदे॒ तव॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Let their arms be confounded, and what thought-and-design is in their heart; let not anything of them be left—in case of thy bite, O Arbudi.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The second pāda is the same with vs. 1 d , above.

items.samhita_patha_plain: मुह्यन्त्वेषां बाहवश्चित्ताकूतं च यद्धृदि। मैषामुच्छेषि किं चन रदिते अर्बुदे तव ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: मुह्यन्तु । एषाम् । बाहव: । चित्तऽआकूतम् । च । यत् । हृदि । मा । एषाम् । उत् । शेषि । किम् । चन । रदिते । अर्बुदे । तव ॥११.१३॥

items.samhita_patha: प्र॑तिघ्ना॒नाः सं धा॑व॒न्तूरः॑ पटू॒रावा॑घ्ना॒नाः। अ॑घा॒रिणी॑र्विके॒श्यो᳡ रुद॒त्यः१॒॑ पुरु॑षे ह॒ते र॑दि॒ते अ॑र्बुदे॒ तव॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Smiting themselves let them (f.) run together, smiting on the breast, the thighs (? paṭāurá ), not anointing, with disheveled hair, wailing when the man is slain, bitten, O Arbudi, of thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Translated by Bloomfield, ib. (see vs. 7). I follow both translators in rendering paṭāurá by 'thigh,' although it is not too acceptable, considering the familiarity of ūru as name for 'thigh.' SPP. reads instead paṭūrāú , with a very small minority of his mss. (of ours, only B.s.m. has it), and with the comm. The latter defines it simply as tat- (i.e. uraḥ ) pradeçāu . He makes aghārin from agha and root ṛ: aghena bhartṛviyogajanitena duḥkhenā ”rtāḥ!

items.samhita_patha_plain: प्रतिघ्नानाः सं धावन्तूरः पटूरावाघ्नानाः। अघारिणीर्विकेश्यो᳡ रुदत्यः१ पुरुषे हते रदिते अर्बुदे तव ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: प्रतिऽघ्नाना: । सम् । धावन्तु । उर: । पटूरौ । आऽघ्नाना: । अघारिणी: । विऽकेश्य᳡: । रुदत्य᳡: । पुरुषे । हते । रदिते ।अर्बुदे । तव ॥११.१४॥

items.samhita_patha: श्व᳡न्वतीरप्स॒रसो॑ रूपका उ॒तार्बु॑दे। अ॑न्तःपा॒त्रे रेरि॑हतीं रि॒शां दु॑र्णिहितै॒षिणी॑म्। सर्वा॒स्ता अ॑र्बुदे॒ त्वम॒मित्रे॑भ्यो दृ॒शे कु॑रूदा॒रांश्च॒ प्र द॑र्शय ॥
items.pada_patha: श्व᳡न्ऽवती: । अ॒प्स॒रस॑: । रूप॑का: । उ॒त । अ॒र्बु॒दे॒ । अ॒न्त॒:ऽपा॒त्रे । रेरि॑हतीम् । रि॒शाम् । दु॒र्नि॒हि॒त॒ऽए॒ष‍िणी॑म् । सर्वा॑: । ता: । अ॒र्बु॒दे॒ । त्वम् । अ॒मित्रे॑भ्य: । दृ॒शे । कु॒रु॒ । उ॒त्ऽआ॒रान् । च॒ । प्र । द॒र्श॒य॒ ॥११.१५॥

commentaries.whitney: Dog-accompanied Apsarases, she-jackals (? rū́pakā ) also, O Arbudi, the riçā́ , licking much in the inner vessel, seeking what is ill-deposited—all these (f.), O Arbudi, do thou make our enemies to see, and do thou show forth specters;—

items.samhita_patha_plain: श्व᳡न्वतीरप्सरसो रूपका उतार्बुदे। अन्तःपात्रे रेरिहतीं रिशां दुर्णिहितैषिणीम्। सर्वास्ता अर्बुदे त्वममित्रेभ्यो दृशे कुरूदारांश्च प्र दर्शय ॥

items.samhita_patha: ख॒डूरे॑ऽधिचङ्क्र॒मां खर्वि॑कां खर्ववा॒सिनी॑म्। य उ॑दा॒रा अ॒न्तर्हि॑ता गन्धर्वाप्स॒रस॑श्च॒ ये स॒र्पा इ॑तरज॒ना रक्षां॑सि ॥
items.pada_patha: ख॒डूरे॑ । अ॒धि॒ऽच॒ङ्क॒माम् । खर्वि॑काम् । ख॒र्व॒ऽवा॒सिनी॑म् । ये । उ॒त्ऽआ॒रा: । अ॒न्त:ऽहि॑ता: । ग॒न्ध॒र्व॒ऽअ॒प्स॒रस॑: । च॒ । ये । स॒र्पा: । इ॒त॒र॒ऽज॒ना: । रक्षां॑सि ॥११.१६॥

commentaries.whitney: Her that strides upon the khaḍū́ra , mutilated, wearing what is mutilated (?); the specters that are concealed, and what Gandharvas-and-Apsarases [there are], serpents, other-folk, demons;—
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. reads at the beginning khadūre , and explains it as ākāçe dūradeçe; our Bp.Kp. have ṣaḍū́re . Again neglecting the accent, he takes adhi and can̄kramām as two independent words. He also reads -vāçinīm in b ; -vāsin might be 'dwelling' (so understood by the Pet. Lexx. and Ludwig). Finally, he reckons the last (irregular) pāda to the following verse. ⌊Pada e = 10. 1 c .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: खडूरेऽधिचङ्क्रमां खर्विकां खर्ववासिनीम्। य उदारा अन्तर्हिता गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्च ये सर्पा इतरजना रक्षांसि ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: खडूरे । अधिऽचङ्कमाम् । खर्विकाम् । खर्वऽवासिनीम् । ये । उत्ऽआरा: । अन्त:ऽहिता: । गन्धर्वऽअप्सरस: । च । ये । सर्पा: । इतरऽजना: । रक्षांसि ॥११.१६॥

items.samhita_patha: चतु॑र्दंष्ट्राञ्छ्या॒वद॑तः कु॒म्भमु॑ष्काँ॒ असृ॑ङ्मुखान्। स्व॑भ्य॒सा ये चो॑द्भ्य॒साः ॥
items.pada_patha: चतु॑:ऽदंष्ट्रान् । श्या॒वऽद॑त: । कु॒म्भऽमु॑ष्कान् । असृ॑क्ऽमुखान् । स्व॒ऽभ्य॒सा: । ये । चे॒ । उ॒त्ऽभ्य॒सा: ॥११.१७॥

commentaries.whitney: The four-tusked ones, the black-toothed, the pot-testicled, the blood-faced; they that are self-frighting and frighting.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The first four epithets are accus. pl. masc.; probably, like the accus. fem. at beginning of vs. 16, objects of prá darçaya 'show forth' in vs. 15. The comm. explains svabhyasās and udbhy- by svāyattabhītayo rākṣaṣāḥ and udgatabhītayaḥ .

items.samhita_patha_plain: चतुर्दंष्ट्राञ्छ्यावदतः कुम्भमुष्काँ असृङ्मुखान्। स्वभ्यसा ये चोद्भ्यसाः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: चतु:ऽदंष्ट्रान् । श्यावऽदत: । कुम्भऽमुष्कान् । असृक्ऽमुखान् । स्वऽभ्यसा: । ये । चे । उत्ऽभ्यसा: ॥११.१७॥

items.samhita_patha: उद्वे॑पय॒ त्वम॑र्बुदे॒ऽमित्रा॑णाम॒मूः सिचः॑। जयां॑श्च जि॒ष्णुश्चा॒मित्राँ॒ जय॑ता॒मिन्द्र॑मेदिनौ ॥
items.pada_patha: उत् । वे॒प॒य॒ । त्वम् । अ॒र्बु॒दे॒ । अ॒मित्रा॑णाम् । अ॒मू: । सिच॑: । जय॑न् । च॒ । जि॒ष्णु: । च॒ । अ॒मित्रा॑न् । जय॑ताम् । इन्द्र॑ऽमेदिनौ ॥११.१८॥

commentaries.whitney: Do thou, O Arbudi, make to tremble yonder lines ( síc ) of our enemies; let both the conquering one and the conqueror, allied with Indra, conquer our enemies.
commentaries.whitney_notes: SPP. reads in his saṁhitā -text jáyāṅç ca in c , with the large majority of his mss., and with part of ours (E.O.s.m.K.). The prolongation being so anomalous, and unsupported by the Prāt., I thinkk jáyaṅç ca decidedly the more acceptable reading. The comm. gives it. He also has çucas for sicas in b . Read amitrāṅ at end of c , with anusvāra -sign, not anunāsika . ⌊Pāda b = 10. 20 b .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: उद्वेपय त्वमर्बुदेऽमित्राणाममूः सिचः। जयांश्च जिष्णुश्चामित्राँ जयतामिन्द्रमेदिनौ ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: उत् । वेपय । त्वम् । अर्बुदे । अमित्राणाम् । अमू: । सिच: । जयन् । च । जिष्णु: । च । अमित्रान् । जयताम् । इन्द्रऽमेदिनौ ॥११.१८॥

items.samhita_patha: प्रब्ली॑नो मृदि॒तः श॑यां ह॒तोऽमित्रो॑ न्यर्बुदे। अ॑ग्निजि॒ह्वा धू॑मशि॒खा जय॑न्तीर्यन्तु॒ सेन॑या ॥

commentaries.whitney: Let our enemy lie squelched, crushed, slain, O Nyarbudi; let tongues of fire, tufts of smoke, go conquering with the army.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. reads in a pravlīnas , in accordance with the more usual form.

items.samhita_patha_plain: प्रब्लीनो मृदितः शयां हतोऽमित्रो न्यर्बुदे। अग्निजिह्वा धूमशिखा जयन्तीर्यन्तु सेनया ॥

commentaries.whitney:
Of our enemies, pushed forth by it, O Arbudi, let Indra, lord of might
( çácīpáti ), slay each best man ( vára ); let no one soever of them be freed.
commentaries.whitney_notes: 'By it'—i.e. by the army; the comm. reads instead tvayā 'by thee.' With a, b compare vi. 67. 2 c, d . ⌊Our d occurs several times: see note to iii. 19. 8.⌋

commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. renders ut kasantu by çarīrād udgacchantu , and ud īṣatu equivalently.

items.samhita_patha: ये च॒ धीरा॒ ये चाधी॑राः॒ परा॑ञ्चो बधि॒राश्च॒ ये। त॑म॒सा ये च॑ तूप॒रा अथो॑ बस्ताभिवा॒सिनः॑। सर्वां॒स्ताँ अ॑र्बुदे॒ त्वम॒मित्रे॑भ्यो दृ॒शे कु॑रूदा॒रांश्च॒ प्र द॑र्शय ॥

commentaries.whitney: Both they who are wise ( dhī́ra ) and they who are unwise, those going away and they who are deaf, they of darkness arid they who are hornless ( tūpará ), likewise those that smell of (?) the goat—all those (m.), O Arbudi, do thou make our enemies to see, and do thou show forth specters.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The meaning of -abhivāsin is wholly uncertain ⌊cf. Pāli vāsita ⌋; the Pet. Lex. conjectures instead -abhivāçin , and the comm. reads bastāvivāçin , as from basta + avi + vāçin . He also, in defiance of pada -text and accent, renders tamasā́s as támasā . ⌊Cf. nabhasá-s (not nábhas-as ), ix. 4. 22.⌋

commentaries.whitney: Let both Arbudi and Trishandhi pierce through our enemies, in order that, O Indra, Vṛitra-slayer, lord of might, we may slay of them, of our enemies, by thousands.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Triṣandhi , lit. 'of three joints,' is conspicuous especially in the next hymn. The comm. explains it here as kaçcit senāmohako devaḥ saṁdhitrayopetavajrāyudhābhimānī vā .

commentaries.whitney: The forest-trees, them of the forest-trees, herbs and plants, Gandharvas-and-Apsarases, serpents, gods, pure-folk ( puṇyajaná ). Fathers—all those, O Arbudi, do thou make our enemies to see, and do thou show forth specters.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. identifies the 'pure-folk' with the yakṣas . ⌊With c, d , cf. viii. 8. 15, above.⌋ ⌊Cf. Kāuç. 73. 5.⌋

items.samhita_patha: ई॒शां वो॑ म॒रुतो॑ दे॒व आ॑दि॒त्यो ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पतिः॑। ई॒शां व॒ इन्द्र॑श्चा॒ग्निश्च॑ धा॒ता मि॒त्रः प्र॒जाप॑तिः। ई॒शां व॒ ऋष॑यश्चक्रुर॒मित्रे॑षु समी॒क्षय॑न्रदि॒ते अ॑र्बुदे॒ तव॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Mastery over you have the Maruts [gained], the heavenly Āditya, Brahmaṇaspati; mastery over you have both Indra and Agni, Dhātar, Mitra, Prajāpati; mastery over you have the seers gained ( kṛ )—exhibiting among the enemies—in case of thy bite, O Arbudi.
commentaries.whitney_notes: One would like to emend devás to devā́s in a .

commentaries.whitney_notes: The mss. set the avasāna in this verse after yūyám , and SPP. very properly does the same. ⌊Our b, c = 2 a, b : b = 10. 1 a .⌋ ⌊The quoted Anukr. says " ye bāhavaḥ ": see vs. 1.⌋
